learningObjectives: Translate application requirements into system components.
Design a layered Java application architecture.
Connect frontend, backend, database, authentication, and external services into a coherent system.

activities.title: Requirement to Component Map
activities.instruction: Explore how requirements translate into system responsibilities.

content.concept: System design starts by identifying users, business requirements, application responsibilities, data, integrations, and constraints before selecting implementation components.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Describe what users need the system to accomplish.
Provides the interface through which users interact with the system.
Processes requests and implements application behavior.
Verifies identity and controls access to protected resources.
Provide capabilities outside the application's core system.

activities.title: Application Architecture Builder
activities.instruction: Build a coherent full-stack Java application architecture.

content.concept: A complete application can connect a client interface to a Java REST backend, business services, persistence, authentication, a database, and optional external integrations.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Request Journey
activities.instruction: Arrange a typical authenticated request through the application.

content.concept: A request can travel from the frontend through authentication and backend layers to business logic and persistence before a response is returned to the client.

activities.title: Technology Choice
activities.instruction: Choose the technology that fits the described responsibility.

content.concept: Technology selection should follow system responsibilities and constraints rather than choosing tools without considering what each layer needs to accomplish.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Spring Boot for implementing a Java REST backend
Relational database for rendering browser buttons
Frontend framework for storing server-side secrets
Git repository as the application's runtime database
